source.title_on_document: AI Use Conditions and Perspective Diversity in Ethical Decision-Making: A Pilot Study of Human Reasoning Processes

supplement.holds: No separate supplement. Appendices A-D (coding manual, participant instructions, scenario, question set) are inside this PDF, pp. 18-30, and hold no further statistics. Data and coding materials are 'available from the author upon reasonable request' (p. 16).

paper_design_summary: Thirty Prolific workers were recruited separately into three conditions (AI-Prohibited, AI-Optional, AI-Mandatory) and answered five open-ended questions about a business ethics dilemma (whether a company should disclose a product defect). One AI-Mandatory participant was dropped for not using AI, leaving 29 (10, 10, 9). Three blind coders counted distinct perspective categories (Perspective Diversity Index) and counterargument categories (Counterargument Diversity Score) in each response; the paper does not say that assignment to conditions was random.

studies.label: Pilot study (ethical dilemma, three AI-use conditions)

assignment.what_was_assigned: AI-use condition: AI prohibited, AI optional, or AI mandatory
assignment.quote: Participants were recruited separately for one of three conditions: • AI-Prohibited • AI-Optional • AI-Mandatory
assignment.locator: p. 5, Section 2.1 Study Design (also abstract, p. 2: 'recruited separately into one of three conditions')

arms.name: AI-Prohibited
arms.description: Told not to use generative AI tools, search engines, or help from other people.

arms.name: AI-Optional
arms.description: Told they could use generative AI tools such as ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini if they wished, and to write final answers in their own words. Of 10, six reported not using AI, one reported using AI as a discussion partner, three did not answer (p. 9, Section 3.2).

arms.name: AI-Mandatory
arms.description: Required to use a generative AI tool before writing final answers and to submit their first AI interaction as evidence; one participant who did not use AI was excluded.

participants.exclusions: 30 participants were recruited. One participant recruited for the AI-Mandatory condition reported not using AI and gave no evidence of AI use, and was excluded from the analysis (p. 5, Section 2.2; p. 9, Section 3.2). The paper does not give per-condition recruitment counts in a table; it reports no randomization, so no randomized count is recorded.
participants.who: Prolific workers with an approval rate of at least 95 percent and 50 to 5,000 prior submissions; demographics were not collected.
participants.country: United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, and Ireland (English-speaking countries)
participants.quote: The final sample consisted of 29 participants: AI-Prohibited (n = 10), AI-Optional (n = 10), AI-Mandatory (n = 9).

ai_tool.name_model: Generative AI tool of the participant's choice, 'such as ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini'; no model or version recorded
ai_tool.how_used: Participants used an outside chatbot on their own before writing answers in their own words; AI-Mandatory participants pasted their first AI exchange as proof of use (pp. 7-8, Section 2.4; Appendix B, pp. 26-27).

task.description: Business ethics dilemma: a middle manager learns the company is hiding a product defect that may have harmed customers; participants answer five open-ended questions on recommended action, stakeholders, counterarguments, risks, and alternative ways to view the problem (pp. 6-7, Section 2.3; Appendices C-D, pp. 28-29).
task.duration: Advertised as approximately 12 minutes, paid 3 pounds (p. 5, Section 2.2)

outcomes.name: Perspective Diversity Index (PDI)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Three blind coders counted the distinct perspective categories (customer, shareholder, employee, management, ethical, legal, regulatory, technical, strategic, social, organizational) in each participant's answer to 'Are there alternative ways to view this problem?'; ICC(2,k) = 0.817 (p. 9, Table 1; coding manual, Appendix A, pp. 18-25).

contrasts.reported: AI-Prohibited n = 10, mean 0.87, SD 0.61; AI-Optional n = 10, mean 0.87, SD 0.67; AI-Mandatory n = 9, mean 2.30, SD 1.72. One-way ANOVA F(2,26) = 5.31, p = .012, eta squared = .290. Cohen's d: AI-Mandatory vs AI-Prohibited 1.13; AI-Mandatory vs AI-Optional 1.12.

outcomes.name: Counterargument Diversity Score (CDS)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Three blind coders counted the distinct counterargument categories (financial, reputation, employee, evidence uncertainty, customer panic, competitive disadvantage, organizational survival) in each participant's answer to 'What arguments could be made against your position?'; ICC(2,k) = 0.868 (p. 9, Table 1; Appendix A, pp. 18-21).

contrasts.reported: AI-Prohibited n = 10, mean 1.47, SD 1.34; AI-Optional n = 10, mean 1.53, SD 0.91; AI-Mandatory n = 9, mean 1.96, SD 1.30. One-way ANOVA F(2,26) = 0.48, p = .626, eta squared = .035.

eligibility.reason: Core eligibility is no because 29 people were analyzed across the three arms (10, 10, 9; 30 recruited), below the 50-person threshold, so criterion 2 is not met (p. 5, Section 2.2). Criterion 1 is unclear: participants were recruited separately, but the allocation mechanism and whether assignment was randomized are not stated (p. 5, Section 2.1; full text and Appendices A-D). Criterion 3 remains unclear: the outcomes are blind-coded counts of perspective and counterargument categories in each person's written response, but the ethical-reasoning task's fit with the creative/ideation scope is uncertain; the paper does not score novelty, originality, usefulness, overall creativity, or similarity across different people's outputs (pp. 6-8, Sections 2.3-2.5; pp. 18-25, Appendix A; creativity-codebook.md, Sections 1 and 6). With quasi_people retained provisionally for the separately recruited groups, context_class is observational under form-spec.md, Field notes for design_class; this mapping does not establish non-random allocation or resolve the task-scope uncertainty.

one_line_finding: In a 29-person Prolific pilot with conditions filled by separate recruitment, the AI-Mandatory group listed more perspective categories than the AI-Prohibited and AI-Optional groups (PDI means 2.30 vs 0.87 and 0.87; F(2,26) = 5.31, p = .012; d = 1.13 vs Prohibited), with no significant difference in counterargument categories (CDS 1.96 vs 1.47 and 1.53; F(2,26) = 0.48, p = .626) (pp. 9-10, Tables 2-3).
